source: twelve relations of the second confirmatory batch, specified from publisher documentation (e3/truth/docs/fresh2/) by three subagents that never saw data, mined FDs or model answers; parts A (benchmarks), B (ChEMBL, MusicBrainz, PLUTO, FHRS), C (GeoNames, EIA-860, STATS19, GHCN)
rule: part A: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. For the three BenchBase benchmarks the DDL at the pinned commit is the specification of the generated data (scale factor 1); a dependency that the H-Store project page states and the DDL neither declares nor contradicts is ambiguous and is recorded with sure: false, quoting both. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part B: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint on a NOT NULL column, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or containment statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out, when two documents conflict, or when a unique index covers a nullable column. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state, and documented non-dependencies, are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part C: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the second confirmatory evaluation, converted by unpack_fresh2.py and joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: BenchBase (benchbase at commit 33c00473807ebd49304d114a6d769d2d2b2bbb34), benchmark tatp, generated into SQLite at scale factor 1 (config/sqlite/sample_tatp_config.xml with <scalefactor>1</scalefactor> instead of the sample's 0.1; the DDL BenchBase applies for SQLite is ddl-generic.sql, which spells the tables SUBSCRIBER, SPECIAL_FACILITY, CALL_FORWARDING in upper case and the columns in lower case; SQLite identifiers are case-insensitive, so each table is exported under its lower-case name), every table exported to benchbase/tatp/<table>.csv with the DDL column names: call_forwarding (root) left-joined to special_facility on (s_id, sf_type) and to subscriber on s_id; dropped bit_3-10, hex_3-10 and byte2_3-10 (random values like the two of each kind that are kept) and the s_id and sf_type of the joined tables, which equal the join columns; access_info, the other one-to-many child of subscriber, is not joined.

cleaning.missing_values: empty and missing references become '?', kept as a value (null = null)

truth.clause: benchbase_tatp_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE CALL_FORWARDING: "PRIMARY KEY (s_id, sf_type, start_time)"; tatp_TATP_Description.pdf, Call_Forwarding Table (p. 5): "Because start_time is part of the primary key, every record must have different start_time."; tatp_TATP_Description.pdf, Appendix A (p. 15): "PRIMARY KEY (s_id, sf_type, start_time)"
truth.justification: (s_id, sf_type, start_time) is the declared primary key of Call_Forwarding, and end_time and numberx are its other columns.

audit.quote: PRIMARY KEY (s_id, sf_type, start_time) ‖ PRIMARY KEY (s_id, sf_type, start_time) ‖ Because start_time is part of the primary key, every record must have different start_time.

truth.clause: benchbase_tatp_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE CALL_FORWARDING: "FOREIGN KEY (s_id, sf_type) REFERENCES SPECIAL_FACILITY (s_id, sf_type)"; benchbase_tatp_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE SPECIAL_FACILITY: "PRIMARY KEY (s_id, sf_type)"; tatp_TATP_Description.pdf, Call_Forwarding Table (p. 5): "s_id and sf_type reference the corresponding fields in the Special_Facility table."; tatp_TATP_Description.pdf, Special_Facility Table (p. 5): "there can only be one record of each sf_type per each subscriber"
truth.justification: (s_id, sf_type) references the declared primary key of Special_Facility, so it identifies one Special_Facility row and its columns.

audit.quote: FOREIGN KEY (s_id, sf_type) REFERENCES SPECIAL_FACILITY (s_id, sf_type) ‖ s_id and sf_type reference the corresponding fields in the Special_Facility table. ‖ PRIMARY KEY (s_id, sf_type) ‖ there can only be one record of each sf_type per each subscriber
audit.source: benchbase_tatp_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE CALL_FORWARDING ‖ tatp_TATP_Description.pdf, Call_Forwarding Table (printed p. 5, PDF page 9) ‖ benchbase_tatp_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE SPECIAL_FACILITY ‖ tatp_TATP_Description.pdf, Special_Facility Table (printed p. 5, PDF page 9)

truth.clause: benchbase_tatp_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE SUBSCRIBER: "s_id         INTEGER     NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY"; benchbase_tatp_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE SPECIAL_FACILITY: "FOREIGN KEY (s_id) REFERENCES SUBSCRIBER (s_id)"; tatp_TATP_Description.pdf, Subscriber Table (p. 4): "s_id is a unique number between 1 and N where N is the number of subscribers (the population size)."; tatp_TATP_Description.pdf, Special_Facility Table (p. 5): "s_id references s_id in the Subscriber table."
truth.justification: s_id is the declared primary key of Subscriber, referenced from Special_Facility (and through it from Call_Forwarding), so it identifies one Subscriber row and its columns.

audit.quote: s_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY ‖ s_id is a unique number between 1 and N where N is the number of subscribers (the population size). ‖ FOREIGN KEY (s_id) REFERENCES SUBSCRIBER (s_id) ‖ s_id references s_id in the Subscriber table.

truth.clause: benchbase_tatp_ddl-generic.sql, CREATE TABLE SUBSCRIBER: "sub_nbr      VARCHAR(15) NOT NULL UNIQUE"; tatp_TATP_Description.pdf, Subscriber Table (p. 4): "sub_nbr is a 15 digit string. It is generated from s_id by transforming s_id to string and padding it with leading zeros."; tatp_TATP_Description.pdf, Appendix A (p. 14): "sub_nbr VARCHAR(15) NOT NULL UNIQUE"
truth.justification: sub_nbr is declared UNIQUE and NOT NULL in Subscriber and is a one-to-one encoding of s_id, so it determines s_id and the other Subscriber columns.

audit.quote: sub_nbr VARCHAR(15) NOT NULL UNIQUE ‖ sub_nbr VARCHAR(15) NOT NULL UNIQUE ‖ sub_nbr is a 15 digit string. It is generated from s_id by transforming s_id to string and padding it with leading zeros. ‖ The sub_nbr column holds a string representation of the s_id number.

gold_design_note: No normalized design is published; the 3NF designs of Sigma* are synthesized.

mined.algorithm: fdmine.py: exact discovery of all minimal FDs in the style of HyFD (no HyFD binary was available); the complete set of minimal FDs is unique, so it equals HyFD's output
